sources.title: Sierra Leone Immigration Department: official eVisa service link
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Sierra Leone Immigration Department homepage on slid.gov.sl identifies its eVisa link as the Official Portal and directs applicants to evisa.sl.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Apply eVisa Official Portal Apply online via the official Sierra Leone eVisa portal.

sources.title: Sierra Leone eVisa: Terms and conditions
sources.publisher: Ministry of Internal Affairs / Sierra Leone Immigration eVisa service
sources.officialityEvidence: SLID links evisa.sl as its official eVisa portal. The portal terms identify the service as the Government of Sierra Leone eVisa system and describe the Ministry of Internal Affairs service, eligible-country rule, emailed approval, entry conditions and visitor scope.
sources.supportingExcerpt: All Countries with exception of all members of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

sources.title: Sierra Leone eVisa: live nationality form selector
sources.officialityEvidence: The official evisa.sl frontend configured by SLID calls this endpoint after nationality selection. The endpoint’s empty JSON response means no current electronic form is exposed for Burkina Faso, despite the terms rule.

sources.title: Sierra Leone eVisa: live Mali nationality-form result
sources.officialityEvidence: The official evisa.sl frontend configured by SLID calls this endpoint after nationality selection. The endpoint’s empty JSON response means no current electronic form is exposed for Mali, despite the terms rule.

sources.title: National Tourist Board: Visa-on-arrival to Sierra Leone
sources.officialityEvidence: The National Tourist Board publishes the 19 November 2019 Government visa-on-arrival announcement on ntb.gov.sl. The page remains live on the current Board site, whose footer says VOA operates, but its issuance date creates a material currency risk. It is retained to explain the unresolved historic cohort, not to normalize a current nationality status.
sources.supportingExcerpt: a new Visa on Arrival policy has been rolled-out for persons from the following countries or blocs

sources.title: Protocol A/P.1/5/79 on free movement of persons, residence and establishment
sources.publisher: Economic Community of West African States Commission
sources.officialityEvidence: ECOWAS publishes the Protocol on its official domain. Article 3 directly establishes visa-free entry for Community citizens visiting a Member State for up to 90 days with the specified travel and health documents.
sources.supportingExcerpt: enter the territory of that Member State free of visa requirements for a maximum period of ninety (90) days.

sources.title: ECOWAS current Member States
sources.publisher: Economic Community of West African States
sources.officialityEvidence: The current ECOWAS member-state page on ecowas.int identifies twelve Member States, including Sierra Leone and eleven foreign catalog passport states.

sources.title: ECOWAS press statement on Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger withdrawal transition
sources.publisher: Economic Community of West African States Commission
sources.officialityEvidence: ECOWAS’s current official press statement says the three withdrawals took effect on 29 January 2025 and requires relevant authorities in and outside ECOWAS Member States to preserve visa-free movement until further notice.
sources.supportingExcerpt: allow citizens of the three affected countries to continue to enjoy the right of visa free movement ... until further notice.

sources.title: Commonwealth: Member countries
sources.officialityEvidence: The Commonwealth Secretariat’s current membership page lists the 56 independent member countries. Together with its official history it confirms that the dated 2019 category cannot safely be expanded to current membership; it is not used to normalize entry status.
sources.supportingExcerpt: 56 independent countries make up the Commonwealth.

sources.title: Commonwealth: membership history
sources.officialityEvidence: The Commonwealth Secretariat’s official history records Maldives’ February 2020 return and Gabon’s and Togo’s June 2022 accessions. This confirms that a dated 2019 category is not a reliable current nationality schedule and is not used to normalize entry status.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Gabon becomes the 55th country to join the Commonwealth in June 2022.

policies.title: Sierra Leone: current ECOWAS ordinary passports — visa-free entry
policies.summary: The ECOWAS Free Movement Protocol establishes visa-free entry for a Community citizen visiting another Member State for up to 90 days. The current ECOWAS roster maps its eleven foreign Member States; the eVisa terms also exclude all ECOWAS members from the electronic service.
conditions: Article 3 requires a valid travel document and international health certificate and gives a maximum 90-day stay. Immigration retains admissibility and public-order controls under the Protocol.
The current twelve-State roster excludes Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger following their withdrawal; the separately documented transitional treatment applies to Burkina Faso and Mali below.
This policy does not decide residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special documents, individual admissibility or any bilateral arrangement.

policies.title: Sierra Leone: Burkina Faso and Mali ordinary passports — ECOWAS transitional visa-free movement
policies.summary: Although Burkina Faso and Mali are no longer shown on ECOWAS’s current twelve-State roster, ECOWAS’s withdrawal transition instruction requires Member-State authorities to continue visa-free movement for their citizens until further notice. Sierra Leone is an ECOWAS Member State.
conditions: This is a temporary ECOWAS transition, not a current membership classification. It remains subject to a contrary later notice, ordinary admission controls, travel-document and health requirements.

The official eVisa nationality endpoints return no electronic form for Burkina Faso and Mali. That operational result is consistent with the transition but is not the legal basis for visa-free status.
It does not establish residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service or special-document treatment.

policies.title: Sierra Leone: non-ECOWAS ordinary passports — advance eVisa
policies.summary: The current official eVisa terms expressly make all countries other than ECOWAS eligible for the electronic visitor visa. This conservative policy applies only to the 87 residual passports not named in the dated 2019 visa-on-arrival announcement; it does not rank the current route for that historic cohort.
conditions: The terms call eVisa a multi-entry electronic travel authorization, send an approved eVisa by email and require a copy at first arrival. It is a genuine advance eVisa, not merely an online form or an optional registration. Legacy portal UI wording about visa issuance at the terminal is inconsistent and should be rechecked, but does not erase the required prior electronic application and emailed approval.

The eVisa is for tourist and business purposes only, valid for one year from issue, normally multiple entry, with a maximum three-month stay and no extension. Passport must have at least six months remaining at entry; all airports and seaports are stated ports.

Biometrics are captured on arrival; funds, health, security, border examination and other entry conditions apply. The eVisa does not authorize paid employment, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service or special-document travel.

Burkina Faso and Mali are excluded here under the current ECOWAS transition; their live official selector has no forms. The dated 2019 visa-on-arrival cohort is deliberately not assigned a current status or route ranking in this policy.

application.label: Sierra Leone Immigration Department eVisa service
application.processingTime: Not established by the reviewed current official terms.
steps: Use the official eVisa portal and select nationality and visa type.
Submit the electronic visa application and payment; approval is notified by email.
Carry the approved eVisa and the same valid passport at arrival for Immigration examination and biometric capture.
